- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.3) in the last 3–5 days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to counteract sentiment-driven downward bias.
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 3–5 days of a new sentiment cycle (e.g., after negative sentiment), especially if sentiment shifts from negative to positive; adjust upward by 1–4%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model shows persistent lag in capturing true price momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if recent 7-day average is rising, or subtract if falling.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1,0,1,0 pattern), model tends to misalign with true volatility; apply smoothing filter to reduce overfitting to sentiment extremes.
